title: Azoth case
description:
**An instance, not a type.** A model declares what a machine *is*; a case declares one machine to run and the answer it must give. The two are separate documents with separate schemas because they answer separate questions, and conflating them is how a spec comes to be edited to fit a test.

A case names the model it instantiates, the components it is made of, the state it is in, and the numbers the run must reproduce. It is a verification instance: the thing a unit test runs. It is not part of the model's contract, and a case that violates the contract is a broken test rather than a discovery about the machine.

model.description: The id of the model this file instantiates. Every case in the file is a run of that model, and a name that resolves to no model is refused rather than ignored - a case file that names nothing is a file nobody is running.

cases.description: One entry per machine to run. Named, because a failing case has to be nameable in a report.

id.description: The case's name, unique within the model. What a failure names.

inputs.description: The instance's inputs, keyed by the model's declared input names. Every one must be declared, and `spec_lint` refuses a key the model does not take.

expected.description: The output values this run must reproduce, keyed by the model's declared output names. A key the model does not declare is refused: an expectation about a field nothing produces is a test of nothing.

tolerance.description: Relative tolerance for every expected value in this case. Stated per case rather than per model because it is a property of the run: a case at a phase boundary is a harder inversion than one deep in a single phase.

source.description: Where the expected values came from, when they did not come from running the model.
